source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment, Ch. 5 (Natural Vegetation).

sections.heading: 1. Natural Vegetation and Forest Types
points: **Natural vegetation** = plant community that has grown naturally without human aid; depends chiefly on **climate (rainfall) and soil**.
India's forests are classified mainly by **rainfall/climate**.

sections.heading: 2. Major Vegetation Types
points: **Tropical Evergreen (Rainforests)** — rainfall >200 cm (Western Ghats, NE India, Andamans); dense, multi-layered; e.g. rosewood, mahogany, ebony.
**Tropical Deciduous (Monsoon forests)** — the **most widespread** in India; rainfall 70–200 cm; shed leaves in dry season; **moist deciduous** (teak, sal) and **dry deciduous** (peepal, neem).
**Tropical Thorn forests** — rainfall <70 cm (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Deccan interior); acacia, babul, cacti; adapted to aridity.
**Montane forests** — vary with altitude (wet temperate, coniferous — pine, deodar, silver fir; then alpine).
**Mangrove (Tidal) forests** — deltas/coasts (**Sundarbans** — Sundari trees); adapted to saline, waterlogged soil.

sections.heading: 3. Forest Conservation and Wildlife
points: **National Forest Policy** aims for **33%** forest cover (much less exists now).
**Reserved, Protected, Unclassed** forests; **social forestry, agro-forestry** programmes.
Wildlife protected via **National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves**; projects like **Project Tiger, Project Elephant**.
India has recognised **Biosphere Reserves** (e.g. Nilgiri, Nanda Devi, Sundarbans).

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Tropical deciduous (monsoon) = most widespread in India; teak, sal.
Tropical evergreen = >200 cm rain (Western Ghats, NE); thorn = <70 cm (Rajasthan).
Mangroves = Sundarbans (Sundari trees); saline, tidal.
National Forest Policy target = 33% forest cover.
Wildlife: National Parks, Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves; Project Tiger.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests are the MOST widespread** in India.
**Tropical evergreen forests need >200 cm rain** (do not shed leaves together).
**Sundarbans mangroves** have **Sundari** trees (saline/tidal).
The **National Forest Policy** targets **33%** forest cover.
